expectations.text: Explains that fresh projects are not yet enabled until the user explicitly chooses a mode
expectations.evidence: Response states: 'the plugin sees this as not yet enabled and prompts you to choose a mode' and 'it will not create any files until you explicitly choose. That's the explicit enablement model. Nothing is activated by just opening the project.'

expectations.text: Offers stealth versus team as the mode choice and explains the difference
expectations.evidence: Response includes a table comparing stealth ('kept local via .git/info/exclude, never committed') and team ('Files go to standard repo paths... and are committed'), plus plain-language guidance: 'Choose stealth if you want opencode-coder for yourself without affecting the repo for others. Choose team if the whole team will use it.'

expectations.text: Explains that startup must not create .coder/ or other artifacts before explicit enablement
expectations.evidence: 'it will not create any files until you explicitly choose. That's the explicit enablement model. Nothing is activated by just opening the project.' — clearly states no artifacts are created pre-enablement.

expectations.text: Mentions .coder/opencode-coder.yaml as where the saved mode lives
expectations.evidence: Response mentions .coder/opencode-coder.yaml multiple times: as the file written by each mode ('echo mode: stealth > .coder/opencode-coder.yaml') and in the verify step ('.coder/opencode-coder.yaml exists with the correct mode').

expectations.text: Explains at least one concrete stealth-versus-team path or git-visibility difference
expectations.evidence: Stealth uses '.git/info/exclude' to keep files local and never committed; team places AGENTS.md and docs/ at repo root and commits them. Verify step also says 'Git visibility matches your chosen mode (stealth = excluded, team = committed)'.

claims.claim: Fresh repos are not yet enabled and init prompts for mode before creating any files
claims.evidence: Explicitly stated in closing summary and in Step 2 description.

claims.claim: Stealth mode uses .git/info/exclude so files are never committed
claims.evidence: Table and Step 3 both describe .git/info/exclude covering .beads/ .opencode/ .coder/ ai.package.yaml.
Shown in both the mode-selection step code blocks and the verify step.

eval_feedback.overall: All five expectations are clearly and substantively met. The response explains explicit enablement, the stealth/team choice with differences, no pre-enablement artifact creation, the .coder/opencode-coder.yaml config file, and concrete path/git-visibility differences between modes. No gaps detected.
